Game collection sources
Historical championship PGNs: PGN Mentor. The 1909 Lasker–Janowski match has a disputed claim to championship status. Fischer–Spassky 1972 and Kramnik–Topalov 2006 forfeits are explicitly marked. Tiebreaks are labeled where the game source identifies them.

THE CHESS JUKEBOX

How to use your jukebox

A front-row seat to chess history. Choose a collection, press play, and let the games unfold.

Getting started

The jukebox starts with the 1886 World Championship and plays the championship collections in order. At the end, it returns to the first game and keeps going. Choose another collection or shuffle in Settings ⚙.

Watching a game

Pause or play. When paused, use the ‹ and › buttons to step back or forward one move.

Jump through a game. Click or tap the progress line to go to a position. Pause first if you want time to study it.

½ – ½

See the result. After the final move, the result appears over the board for twice the selected move time. Pause during that display to study or step back; the result disappears when you go back.

For a recorded forfeit, the result and FORFEIT appear over the starting board. Names, location, date, game type and clock times appear when available in the game record; a silhouette stands in for an unavailable portrait.

Evaluation bar

Use Evaluation on the main page to turn the bar on or off. Your choice carries over to the next game or collection. Stockfish analyzes each position on your device, and the bar shows which side it favors. White means White; black means Black. Flip the board and the bar flips with it. The evaluation can keep changing while a game is paused. If the engine cannot run on your device, the jukebox keeps playing without it.

The engine uses Stockfish.js, licensed under GPLv3.

Game buttons

FLIP BOARD ↕Turn the board around. Each new game begins with White at the bottom.
RESTART GAME ↺Return to this game’s starting position.
NEXT GAME →Go to the next game in the collection’s order, even when shuffle is selected.
NEXT COLLECTION →Move between championship collections and wrap back to the first; select other collections in Settings.

Choose what plays

Open Settings ⚙. Under Game collection, choose all world championships, all non-championship collections, all collections, or an individual collection. Choose In order or Shuffle, without repeats, and adjust Seconds per move. Select Start playing to apply your choices and start the selected collection.

Automatic playback follows the chosen collection and loops within it. All World Championship Collections does not include Gukesh–Sindarov; All Collections does.

Bring your own games

In Settings, select Choose PGN and choose a file containing one game or a collection, then select Start playing. The jukebox supports standard-chess games; unsupported variants and unmarked games without moves are skipped. A no-move game with a recorded result and [Termination "forfeit"] is shown as a forfeit. Your browser may remember the imported file on this device, subject to its storage limits.

Match scores and controls

For supported two-player championship matches, the score beside the players shows the match score before the game, then updates after its last move. Rapid tiebreak scores are shown separately where identified. Tournament and imported games may not have a match score.

On a computer, the space bar pauses or resumes when the page itself has focus; while paused, the left and right arrows step through moves. On a TV, use the browser’s remote or pointer to select the controls.
